front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose

**[AGENCY NAME]** (the "Agency") operates as a DODD-licensed residential facility under ORC 5123.19 and OAC Chapter 5123-3. It is also a DODD-certified, Medicaid-enrolled HCBS provider under the Individual Options (IO) waiver, delivering Homemaker/Personal Care (OAC 5123-9-30) and Shared Living (OAC 5123-9-33).

This Policy & Procedure Manual does four things:

1. **Sets out the Agency's written policies and procedures.** OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b) requires them. They cover person-centered planning, satisfaction, internal monitoring, staff supervision, the training plan, service delivery, background investigations, and volunteers if used.
2. **Documents the Agency's internal compliance program.** The program covers Chapter 5123-3, background investigations, service delivery, documentation and billing, and management of individuals' funds (OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c)-(d)).
3. **Protects the people we serve.** It safeguards their rights under ORC 5123.62 and gives staff clear steps for health, safety, incident reporting, behavior support, and transfer or termination.
4. **Gives DODD reviewers a single source.** DODD can use it during the pre-license survey, compliance reviews, and HCBS certification to see how the Agency meets each applicable rule.

The Agency may not operate a residential facility, or admit a person with a developmental disability to one, without a DODD license (ORC 5123.20). The Agency must keep its license, its ODM Medicaid provider agreement, and its HCBS approval in good standing.

# How to Use This Manual

**Who should use it.** The governing body, administrator, supervisors, direct support professionals (DSPs), support staff, and volunteers (if used) should all use this manual. Each person should know the sections that apply to their role.

**Customize before use.** This manual is a template. Before adoption, the Agency must:
- Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and all other bracketed fields with Agency-specific information, such as names, addresses, titles, phone numbers, licensed capacity, and services offered.
- Delete or adapt any section that does not match the Agency's services. For example, remove Shared Living content if the Agency does not provide it.
- Confirm that each procedure matches what the Agency actually does. Do not adopt a procedure the Agency cannot follow.

**Adopt it.** The Agency's governing body must formally adopt the customized manual and record the adoption date and approval in its minutes. The governing board also reviews annual audit or financial statements and compliance review reports and plans of correction. It monitors the internal compliance program and promotes high-quality services (OAC 5123-3-01(C)(6)).

**Keep it current.** Review the manual at least annually. Also review it whenever a rule changes, DODD issues a compliance review finding, or Agency operations change. Record the revision date and approver for each change. Keep a copy at each facility where staff can reach it, and keep superseded versions on file.

**Train staff.** Every staff member must be trained on the policies relevant to their role. Training must happen before they work independently and again when policies change. Record each training's description, date, duration, and instructor, and keep the written training plan updated at least every 12 months (OAC 5123-3-01(D)(6)-(8)). Staff should sign an acknowledgment that they have received and understand the manual.

**Appendix A.** Appendix A maps every item on the official review documents to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to prepare for a DODD review and to confirm no required item is missing.

**Check the source rules.** This manual summarizes rules in operational terms. The rules themselves control. Where this manual and a rule differ, follow the rule and correct the manual.

## Official review documents

Ohio has **no single DODD policy checklist or form** for reviewing a residential facility's policy manual. DODD instead reviews the Agency against the rule text itself, and Appendix A is organized around these official documents:

- **OAC 5123-3-01**, Licensed residential facilities - administration and operation (effective 9/29/2024). Paragraph (C)(5)(b) lists the required written policies. Paragraph (C)(5)(c) covers the internal compliance program, and paragraph (D) covers the training plan and personnel policies.
- **OAC 5123-3-02**, Physical environment standards, fire safety, and emergency response planning. Paragraph (F) supplies the fire safety and emergency response plan.
- **OAC 5123-3-04**, Admission of residents, provision of services, and maintenance of service records. It covers admission, medication disposal, transportation, food, clothing and belongings, and records and confidentiality.
- **OAC 5123-3-05**, Transfer and termination of services. Paragraph (C) is titled "Transfer and termination of services policies."
- **DODD Residential Facility Development Application (with checklist)**, updated 8/1/15, no form number. This is used for development approval under OAC 5123-3-08. It lists inspections and application paperwork rather than policy content, so Appendix A takes no items from it.

**Appendix A** maps every official item from these documents to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Where a rule requires an explicit written policy, procedure, or plan, Appendix A marks it as written. Other items are practice requirements that the manual addresses.

DODD's compliance review under OAC 5123-3-06 includes an examination of the facility's policies. An abbreviated review focuses on background checks, behavioral support, medication administration, major unusual incidents, and service delivery.

## Adoption and maintenance

- **Customize.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholders and bracketed fields before use.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the adoption.
- **Keep current.** Review at least annually and whenever rules, findings, or operations change.
- **Train.** All staff must be trained on the manual, with training documented under OAC 5123-3-01(D)(6)-(8).

citations.title: Operation of residential facilities
citations.requirement: Apply for the license to the DODD director. DODD does a pre-license survey and gives local officials notice; it cannot issue the license until 10 days (excluding weekends/holidays) after mailing. Initial license ≤1 year, renewal ≤3 years.

citations.title: Prohibiting operation without license
citations.requirement: No one may operate a residential facility, or admit a person with a developmental disability to one, without a DODD license.

citations.title: License not transferable; posting
citations.requirement: License is valid only for the licensee, the named premises, the number of individuals on it, and its term. It is not transferable. Keep it at the facility and show it to anyone on request.

citations.title: Licensee/operator contract
citations.requirement: A licensee may contract with another entity as operator. They need a written agreement requiring the operator to give the licensee the information it needs; the licensee stays responsible for compliance with all rules.

citations.title: HCBS approval and Medicaid provider agreement
citations.requirement: If HCBS is delivered in the facility, submit the DODD application for approval, keep an ODM Medicaid provider agreement, and follow the Chapter 5123-9 rule for each HCBS delivered.

citations.title: Licensee notifications to DODD
citations.requirement: Notify DODD electronically within 14 days of disqualifying-offense charges/convictions, related-party status, a new 5%+ financial interest, or an administrator license suspension; within 7 days of bankruptcy. Keep contact info current.

citations.title: Financial and insurance proof
citations.requirement: At application and on request, show a $10,000 line of credit or a $10,000 daily bank balance for 90 days, plus a general liability certificate of at least $1,000,000 covering individuals' theft/property damage losses.

citations.title: Operator compliance and rights safeguards
citations.requirement: Comply with Chapter 5123-3 and applicable federal, state and local law (ADA, fire code, wage and hour, workers' comp, unemployment, withholding). Safeguard rights under ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65 and meet 5123.63 and 5123.64.

citations.title: Required written policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Written policies are required on person-centered planning, satisfaction, internal monitoring, staff supervision, the training plan, service delivery, background investigations (5123-2-02), and volunteers if used.

citations.title: Internal compliance program
citations.requirement: Show an internal compliance program covering Chapter 5123-3, background investigations, service delivery/documentation/billing, and management of individuals' funds. Take part in DODD data collection when asked.

citations.title: Governing board duties
citations.requirement: A governing board must review annual audit or financial statements, review compliance review reports and plans of correction, monitor the internal compliance program, and promote high-quality services.

citations.title: Background investigations; Rapback; annual abuser-registry notice
citations.requirement: Run 5123-2-02 background checks. The administrator, and a natural-person licensee or operator, must consent to Rapback. Each year give staff written notice of conduct that leads to abuser registry placement and of the 14-day charge-reporting duty.

citations.title: Payroll compliance; staff on duty; support staff
citations.requirement: Stay current on payroll taxes, workers' comp and unemployment premiums. Schedule staff on duty by individuals' needs, with schedules prepared in advance and available at each facility. Provide enough support staff that DSPs are not pulled from primary duties.

citations.title: Personnel records, training plan, training records
citations.requirement: Keep personnel records. Keep a written training plan (competency method; responsible person; timelines) updated at least every 12 months. Record each training's description, date, duration and instructor.

citations.title: Administrator requirements
citations.requirement: Employ an administrator aged 21+ who meets the experience and education tiers. Designate an acting delegate in writing. Notify DODD within 14 days of an administrator change; orientation within 30 days; report if serving more than one licensee.

citations.title: DSP requirements
citations.requirement: DSPs must be 18+ and read/write English. Within 60 days of hire they need Red Cross-equivalent first aid and CPR with in-person skills assessment. Until then they work only with a certified staff present. Appendix B training applies.

citations.title: Supervisor, support staff and direct support assistant requirements
citations.requirement: Supervisors meet the DSP requirements and complete supervisor training within 90 days of becoming a supervisor. Support staff complete appendix C training. Direct support assistants (age 16-17) have limited duties with a DSP.

citations.title: Physical environment standards
citations.requirement: Accessible, clean, safe, homelike. Annual fire inspection; carbon monoxide detector if gas furnace/water heater; 80 sq ft living area per person; max 2 per bedroom (80/120 sq ft); 1:4 bath ratio; free phone access; no signage labeling residents.

citations.title: Fire safety and emergency response plan; equipment
citations.requirement: Have a fire safety and emergency response plan approved by state/local authority and shared with the county board. Post floor plans; keep exits clear; extinguisher on each floor. Facilities with 5 or fewer need smoke detectors on each floor.

citations.title: Fire and tornado drills; training; emergency reports
citations.requirement: Document 3 fire drills per 12 months (morning, afternoon/evening, asleep) and 1 tornado drill. Train each individual within 30 days of residency and yearly. Report any fire with fire department response to DODD within 1 business day.

citations.title: Person-centered planning
citations.requirement: Individuals (or guardians) make decisions about services. For non-ICF homes the county board SSA coordinates assessment and develops the ISP under OAC 5123-4-02; the operator participates and implements the plan.

citations.title: Admission of residents
citations.requirement: Admission is voluntary with informed consent. Admit only those whose needs can be met. Give written admission decision within 30 days of application; notify the county board within 14 days of admitting a resident.

citations.title: Standards of service provision
citations.requirement: Staff provide person-centered services and know the ISP before serving. They take reasonable steps to prevent incidents and follow 5123-2-06. DSPs must not serve their own minor child or spouse, or be impaired by alcohol/drugs on duty.

citations.title: Health care, medication, and disposal
citations.requirement: Medication administration, nurse delegation and medication error reporting follow Chapters 5123-6 and 5123-17. Written disposal procedures need two-staff verification. Medication accounting is due within 24 hours of a death and by the last day of residency on termination.

citations.title: Transportation
citations.requirement: Driver must hold a valid license and liability insurance. Obtain a BMV driving record within 14 days before hire and every 3 years. Drivers with 6+ points are prohibited. Written vehicle accessibility/maintenance/driver policies.

citations.title: Food, clothing and personal belongings
citations.requirement: Offer daily meals and snacks that meet nutritional needs and preferences. Modified/therapeutic diets follow physician or dietitian instructions. Keep 3 days fresh and 5 days staple food. Inventory belongings within 14 days of admission when assessed need.

citations.title: Individuals' service records
citations.requirement: Keep current records at the facility: photograph, legal status, ISP with documented informed consent, and signed authorization to seek medical treatment (or documented attempts). The fetched text was truncated; confirm the remaining items.

citations.title: Transfer and termination grounds and notice
citations.requirement: Initiate transfer/termination only on listed grounds. Give 30 days' written notice by certified mail to the individual and county board, including appeal rights and Disability Rights Ohio contact. Services continue during a hearing unless an emergency exists.

citations.title: Transfer/termination appeal, mediation and hearing
citations.requirement: Appeal to governing board/administrator within 7 days of notice; decision within 5 days; appeal to the DODD director within 5 days. DODD mediation within 15 days, then hearing within 30 days; burden of proof is on the operator.

citations.title: Compliance reviews, summary, appeal and plan of correction
citations.requirement: DODD reviews at least once per license term; special reviews may be unannounced. Summary within 10 days of the review ending. Appeal or plan of correction within 14 days of receipt; DODD acts within 10 days (appeal) or 20 days (plan).

citations.title: License issuance and adverse actions
citations.requirement: Three-year license issued within 20 days of compliance and fee collection; one-year license if adverse action needs a plan of correction. DODD may suspend admissions, place a monitor, or refuse to renew/revoke. Notify residents and guardians within 3 business days.

citations.title: Development and renovation; development approval
citations.requirement: Obtain DODD development approval before applying for a residential facility license. DODD will not approve licensed beds exceeding the statutory limit.

citations.title: MUI: immediate reporting and protective measures
citations.requirement: Employees immediately report suspected or actual major unusual incidents to the provider's designee, the county board, or the DODD hotline. The provider immediately secures medical care and removes staff alleged in physical or sexual abuse from contact.

citations.title: MUI: county board notice and incident report deadlines
citations.requirement: Notify the county board within 4 hours of discovery of abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation, peer-to-peer acts, prohibited sexual relations, unexplained death, or media inquiry. Submit the incident report by 3 p.m. the next working day.

citations.title: MUI categories A, B, C and unusual incidents
citations.requirement: Category A: abuse, neglect, exploitation, death unexplained. Category B: suicide attempt, natural death, medical emergency, missing individual, peer-to-peer, significant injury. Category C: law enforcement, hospitalization, unapproved behavior support.

citations.title: Incident report content
citations.requirement: Incident reports include the individual's name and address, date/time/location, who/what/when/where description, injuries, immediate actions, persons involved, witness statements, notifications, medical follow-up, and the author's signature.

citations.title: MUI scope for round-the-clock services
citations.requirement: For individuals receiving round-the-clock waiver services, all MUIs are reported wherever they occur. Certain types are reported wherever they occur; others only when the individual is being served by the provider.

citations.title: Prohibited measures
citations.requirement: Never use prone restraint, restraint that restricts breathing or causes pain, disabling a communication device, meal denial, dark rooms, painful sound, shock, humiliating treatment, or restrictive measures for punishment or convenience.

citations.title: Restrictive measures: limits
citations.requirement: Chemical/manual/mechanical restraint, rights restriction and time-out are last resort, only for risk of harm (or legal sanction for rights restriction). Time-out: max 30 minutes per incident, 1 hour per 24 hours, never key-locked, constant visual supervision.

citations.title: Behavioral support strategy development
citations.requirement: Use positive measures first. Restrictive measures require documentation positives failed, an assessment within 12 months, a qualified author, informed consent, human rights committee approval, guardian notification terms, and review every 90 days.

citations.title: Chapter 5123-6 definitions: health-related activities and medication errors
citations.requirement: Defines health-related activities (13 listed tasks), delegable nursing tasks, delegating nurse, employer oversight, and medication/treatment error types, including administration by uncertified personnel or without required nursing delegation.

citations.title: HPC provider qualifications
citations.requirement: HPC is delivered only by an independent or agency provider with an ODM Medicaid provider agreement. Licensed providers must keep the 5123.19 license and the Medicaid agreement. Noncompliance may lead to license or certification action.

citations.title: HPC service delivery requirements
citations.requirement: Serve per an ISP under 5123-4-02. No HPC with money management or shared living for the same person. Arrange approved substitute coverage. Use EVV for 15-minute units. Agencies need a documented overtime review process.

citations.title: HPC service documentation
citations.requirement: Document service type, date, place, individual and Medicaid ID, provider and contract number, signature/initials, group size, description tied to the ISP, units or time, and start/stop times.

citations.title: HPC group-size rate adjustments
citations.requirement: One staff serving two individuals: base rate 107% of one-to-one; three individuals 117%; four or more 130%. Rate is divided among those served. Rates by county cost-of-doing-business category.

citations.title: On-site/on-call definition
citations.requirement: On-site/on-call applies only when the individual is expected to be asleep at least 5 continuous hours and the provider is present and available but need not stay awake. It may not be authorized in the provider's own residence.

citations.title: Rights of persons with a developmental disability
citations.requirement: Rights include dignity, privacy, free communication, personal possessions, managing finances by ability, confidentiality of records, grievances without reprisal, freedom from unnecessary restraint, abuse-free living, medical access, and voting.

citations.title: HCBS waivers - shared living
citations.requirement: Shared living is a distinct service: no more than 4 persons with DD in a home where it is delivered; a group of two is paid at 85% of the daily rate. Not combined with HPC for the same individual.

citations.title: Agency provider certification
citations.requirement: Agency providers need a certificate of general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 and proof of an unencumbered $10,000 line of credit or bank balance for certification.

citations.title: Individual Options waiver
citations.requirement: DODD operates the Individual Options waiver under an interagency agreement with ODM.

citations.title: Background investigations: pre-hire requirements
citations.requirement: Before hire: application, reference attempts, check 7 databases (OIG, abuser registry, nurse aide, sex offender, SAM, ODM exclusion, DRC offender); no hire if listed in (C)(2)(a)-(f). Signed attestation and 14-day charge-notice agreement. Driving record for drivers.

citations.title: Criminal records check, conditional employment, Rapback, 5-year recheck
citations.requirement: Request BCII check (FBI check if not an Ohio resident for 5 years). Conditional employment max 60 days; terminate on day 61 if no result. Enroll DSPs in Rapback within 14 days; recheck databases at least every 5 years.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, Self-Determination and Community Integration
policies.applies_to: All residents of the licensed residential facility and all individuals served under the Individual Options (IO) waiver; the administrator, supervisors, direct support professionals (DSPs), and all other staff and volunteers
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual served by [AGENCY NAME] directs the decisions about his or her own services, that services are built on the individual service plan (ISP) developed with the county board, and that each person has real opportunities to take part in community life and employment.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b)(i) — Written policies and procedures that address management practices regarding person-centered planning and self-determination. [AGENCY NAME] recognizes that individuals, or their guardians where a guardian has authority, make the decisions about their services. For homes that are not ICF-licensed, the county board of developmental disabilities service and support administrator (SSA) coordinates the assessment and develops the ISP under OAC 5123-4-02. [AGENCY NAME] participates in that process and implements the ISP as written. No staff member may provide a service to an individual until he or she has read and understands that individual's current ISP. The community activities and employment options offered to each individual are documented as the ISP directs. This policy supports the person-centered planning and community integration expectations of 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: The written plan developed by the county board SSA with the individual (and guardian, if any) and the team under OAC 5123-4-02. It describes the individual's outcomes, services and supports.
A planning process led by the individual that reflects his or her preferences, strengths, goals and choices and the supports needed to reach them.
The individual's right to make choices and decisions about his or her own life and services, with the support of a guardian or chosen advocate where applicable.
The county board employee who coordinates assessment and develops and monitors the ISP.
Access to and participation in community life, activities, relationships and employment in the same way as people without disabilities, as the ISP directs.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator or designee asks the county board SSA for the current ISP and the most recent assessment. The admission is not completed until a current ISP is on file (see AM-01).

The Administrator or designee explains to the individual and guardian, in accessible language and in the format they prefer, that they decide about services, and gives them the name and phone number of the SSA.

The Administrator or a supervisor attends or participates in each ISP meeting, annual and revision, as invited by the SSA. The Administrator or supervisor brings the facility's observations about the individual's preferences, progress, health and any concerns.
Within 5 business days after receiving a new or revised ISP, the supervisor reviews it with the Administrator and writes any needed changes to the individual's daily routine or staff assignments.

Before working alone with an individual, each DSP reads that individual's ISP and signs and dates a statement that he or she has read it and had questions answered. The supervisor keeps the signed statement in the staff training record (see ST-04).

When an ISP is revised, the supervisor notifies all staff assigned to that individual and each DSP re-signs the acknowledgment for the changed sections before the next shift in which he or she works alone with the individual.

Staff ask each individual daily, in the way the individual communicates best, about choices such as wake and sleep times, meals, clothing, activities, visitors and use of personal space. Staff honor those choices unless the ISP or a documented rights restriction under IR-02 provides otherwise.

If an individual's choice appears to conflict with health or safety, staff do not override it on their own. Staff discuss the risk with the individual and guardian, inform the supervisor, and ask the SSA to convene the team to address the matter in the ISP.

The supervisor makes sure each outcome and action step in the ISP assigned to [AGENCY NAME] has a written daily or weekly implementation method, and that staff record progress or the reason an activity did not occur.

The supervisor reviews, at least monthly, the community activities and employment options offered to each individual against what the ISP directs. The review is documented in the individual's service record, including the activity or option offered, the date, the individual's response, and any barrier (such as transportation or staffing).
The Administrator arranges transportation and staffing so that individuals can take part in community activities and employment on the schedule they chose (see TR-01 and ST-02).
If an individual declines an activity or employment option, staff record the choice, do not pressure the individual, and re-offer the option at reasonable intervals as the ISP directs.
The supervisor reports to the SSA within 3 business days any need for a change in the ISP, such as a change in preferences, health, behavior, or a service that cannot be provided as written.
The Administrator checks implementation of person-centered planning at least annually through the internal monitoring process in MP-02, and the results are reported to the governing board.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures ISPs are on file, staff are trained on them, ISP outcomes are implemented, and the facility participates in planning meetings.
Reviews each ISP with staff, obtains DSP acknowledgments, monitors daily implementation and monthly community and employment option documentation.
Reads the ISP before serving, offers and honors choices, implements ISP outcomes, and documents services and the individual's responses.
Makes decisions about services and participates in ISP development and review.
Coordinates assessment, develops, monitors and revises the ISP under OAC 5123-4-02.

documentation: Current ISP and assessment for each individual in the service record
Signed DSP ISP acknowledgment statements
Notes of ISP meetings attended and changes made to routines or staff assignments
Monthly record of community activities and employment options offered, with the individual's response
Daily or weekly ISP outcome progress notes
Notices to the SSA of needed ISP changes

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Individual Satisfaction, Internal Monitoring and Evaluation
policies.applies_to: All individuals served, the Administrator, supervisors, DSPs, the designated compliance officer, and the governing board
policies.purpose: To find out whether individuals are satisfied with the services [AGENCY NAME] delivers, to monitor and evaluate the quality of those services, and to correct problems promptly with oversight from the governing board.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b)(ii) — Individuals' satisfaction with services delivered; and OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b)(iii) — Internal monitoring and evaluation procedures to improve services delivered. [AGENCY NAME] collects satisfaction input from each individual at least annually and acts on it. It uses internal monitoring to identify and correct service problems. As a matter of internal practice, it trends major unusual incidents (MUIs), deaths and medication errors for the governing board. The governing board reviews annual audit or financial statements, reviews compliance review reports and plans of correction, monitors the internal compliance program (IC-01), and promotes high-quality services as required by OAC 5123-3-01(C)(6). [AGENCY NAME] takes part in DODD data collection when asked, as required by OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(d).

definitions.definition: Information gathered from an individual (and guardian or chosen advocate) about how satisfied he or she is with the services, staff, home, choices and community access.
Planned, recurring reviews by [AGENCY NAME] of its own services, records and environment to find and fix problems.
An incident category defined by DODD rule that must be reported and investigated; see BP-03.
A written plan [AGENCY NAME] submits in response to compliance review findings, describing how and when each deficiency will be corrected.
The body with ultimate authority over [AGENCY NAME], described in GOV-01.

procedures: The Administrator designates a compliance officer ([COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME]) to coordinate satisfaction collection and internal monitoring and to report to the governing board.

At least once every 12 months, and sooner when requested, the supervisor collects satisfaction input from each individual using a short survey or interview about staff treatment, choices, food, privacy, activities, health care and safety.

The survey is offered in the individual's preferred communication method. The individual may choose a person who is not a DSP serving him or her (for example, a guardian, family member, advocate or SSA) to help answer, and the survey does not require the individual to sign if he or she does not wish to.
Guardians and, with the individual's permission, family members may also give input. The record shows whose input it is.

Within 30 days after collection, the Administrator reviews all responses, identifies dissatisfaction or requests, and writes an action response for each: what will change, who is responsible and the date. The Administrator reports back to the individual what was done.
Complaints raised in surveys are handled under IR-03 and any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately under BP-02.

Each month, the supervisor completes an internal monitoring checklist covering: ISP implementation, service documentation, medication records, staff schedules versus staff on duty, drills, environmental safety, individual funds records and rights restrictions.
Each quarter, the compliance officer completes a deeper review of a sample of individual records and personnel files and compares findings with prior quarters.
Any deficiency identified is entered on a corrective action log with the date found, person responsible, due date and date verified as fixed. The Administrator verifies the fix and signs the log.

Each quarter, the compliance officer prepares a trend report of MUIs, unusual incidents, deaths, medication errors, grievances and corrective actions, and identifies patterns by individual, staff, time or location.
The Administrator presents the quarterly trend report, satisfaction results and corrective action log to the governing board at its next meeting. The minutes record the discussion and decisions.

The governing board reviews the annual audit or financial statements, each compliance review report and plan of correction, and the internal compliance program reports, and directs actions to promote high-quality services. The board's review is recorded in the minutes.
When DODD requests data or participation in data collection, the Administrator assigns responsibility, responds by the requested date and keeps a copy of what was submitted.
The Administrator reviews this policy and the monitoring tools at least annually and updates them based on findings (see GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews audits, compliance review reports and plans of correction; monitors the internal compliance program; promotes high-quality services.
Ensures satisfaction collection, monitoring, corrective action and board reporting occur and respond to DODD data requests.
Coordinates reviews, maintains the corrective action log and prepares quarterly trend reports.
Collects satisfaction input, completes monthly monitoring checklists and carries out corrective actions.
May give satisfaction input and raise concerns at any time without retaliation.

documentation: Annual satisfaction surveys or interview notes and action responses
Monthly internal monitoring checklists
Quarterly record reviews
Corrective action log
Quarterly trend reports (MUIs, deaths, medication errors, grievances)
Governing board minutes showing review of audits, compliance review reports and plans of correction
Copies of DODD data submissions

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Supervision of Staff
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, supervisors of DSPs, DSPs, support staff, direct support assistants and volunteers
policies.purpose: To make sure all staff are supervised by qualified, trained supervisors who observe performance and competency, correct problems and see that individuals' needs are met on every shift.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b)(iv) — Supervision of staff. Supervisors of DSPs must meet the DSP requirements and must complete supervisor training within 90 days of becoming a supervisor (OAC 5123-3-01(G)-(I)). Supervision, including observation of competency and performance, is documented. Staff on duty are scheduled according to the needs of the individuals, with schedules prepared in advance and available at each facility, and enough support staff are provided so DSPs are not pulled from their primary duties (OAC 5123-3-01(D)(3)-(5)).

definitions.definition: A person designated by [AGENCY NAME] to direct, observe and evaluate the work of DSPs and other staff.
The training DODD requires of a new supervisor, to be completed within 90 days of becoming a supervisor.
Direct observation of a staff member performing a task to confirm he or she can do it correctly and safely.
Staff such as cooks, housekeepers, maintenance and drivers who perform tasks other than direct support so DSPs can remain with individuals.

procedures: The Administrator names a supervisor for each shift and each location and posts the supervisor's name and phone number ([PHONE]) where all staff can see it. A supervisor or on-call supervisor is reachable at all times that individuals are served.
Before a person is named supervisor, the Administrator confirms that he or she meets the DSP qualifications (ST-05) and has a completed background investigation under MP-05.

The Administrator enrolls each new supervisor in the required supervisor training on the date of appointment, records the 90-day completion deadline and verifies completion. If a supervisor has not completed the training by day 90, the Administrator removes the supervisory duties until it is completed.
Each new DSP is observed by a supervisor on the job during his or her first shifts and is not left to work alone until the supervisor documents competency in the tasks assigned (see ST-04).

The supervisor observes each DSP performing duties at least monthly for the first 90 days of employment and at least quarterly afterward, including medication tasks, mealtime support, transportation, documentation, interactions with individuals, and following of ISPs and behavior support plans.
The supervisor completes a written observation form each time with the date, tasks observed, strengths, concerns, coaching given and follow-up date. The DSP and supervisor sign it.

If a DSP is not competent in a task, the supervisor retrains and re-observes before the DSP does the task independently. Medication administration or delegated nursing tasks are not performed by anyone not certified or delegated (HC-01, HC-02).
The supervisor reviews service documentation, daily logs and medication records at least weekly for completeness and accuracy and corrects issues with the staff member.

The Administrator prepares staff schedules in advance based on each individual's assessed needs, ISP and activities. The schedule shows who is on duty each shift, is kept at each facility and is made available for review (see ST-02).

The Administrator provides enough support staff, such as housekeeping, cooking and maintenance, so DSPs are not pulled from primary duties. A supervisor who sees a DSP being pulled away from direct support reports it to the Administrator the same day.

Staff must report any observed or suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation or incident immediately to the supervisor and as required by BP-02 and BP-03. A supervisor who receives a report does not delay it for any reason.

The supervisor documents performance concerns, coaching and corrective action in the personnel record, and recommends to the Administrator discipline up to termination when needed (see PS-01 and ST-03).
The Administrator reviews each supervisor's observation records at least quarterly and reports supervision findings to the governing board through the process in MP-02.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints qualified supervisors, ensures supervisor training is completed in 90 days, schedules staff by individual needs and provides support staff.
Observes and documents staff competency and performance, reviews documentation, retrains, coaches and reports concerns.
Works under supervision, accepts coaching, performs only tasks for which competency is documented and reports concerns.
Reviews supervision findings and staffing adequacy reported by the Administrator.

documentation: Supervisor designation list and posted coverage schedule
Supervisor qualification and training completion records with dates
Staff observation and competency forms
Weekly documentation review notes
Staff schedules prepared in advance and kept at each facility
Coaching and corrective action records in personnel files

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Service Delivery
policies.applies_to: All staff and volunteers who provide or support services to individuals in the residential facility and under the IO waiver
policies.purpose: To make sure services are person-centered, follow each individual's ISP, protect individuals from preventable harm and meet the rules that apply to the specific service delivered.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b)(vi) — Service delivery. Services provided by [AGENCY NAME] are person-centered and follow the ISP. Staff know the ISP before serving an individual. Staff take reasonable steps to prevent major unusual incidents and unusual incidents. Any behavior support strategy follows OAC 5123-2-06. A DSP must not serve his or her own minor child or spouse, and must not be impaired by alcohol or drugs while on duty (OAC 5123-3-04(D)). Where a home and community-based service is delivered, [AGENCY NAME] also follows the Chapter 5123-9 rule for that service (see HCBS-01 and HCBS-02). The ISP is developed under OAC 5123-4-02 and implemented as written (OAC 5123-3-03).

definitions.definition: A service that reflects the individual's preferences, choices, goals and communication style as recorded in the ISP.
An event involving an individual that is not part of routine operations and must be recorded and reviewed under BP-03.
A more serious category of incident defined in DODD rules and reported under BP-03.
A planned approach to address behavior, which must follow OAC 5123-2-06 and BP-01.
Under the influence of alcohol or drugs to the degree that the person's ability to provide safe services is reduced.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the current ISP of each individual at the facility where staff can read it and make sure that the ISP is accessible to all staff assigned to the individual.
Each DSP reads the ISP and signs the acknowledgment (MP-01) before providing services to that individual. A supervisor does not assign a DSP to an individual whose ISP he or she has not read.
Staff deliver services at the times, in the places and in the manner described in the ISP, and offer choices at every opportunity (MP-01).

At the start of each shift, the supervisor or lead DSP briefs staff on each individual's current needs, health changes, appointments, new orders, incidents on the prior shift and any safety precautions.

Staff take reasonable steps to prevent incidents, including following each individual's risk and safety plans, supervising at the level in the ISP, keeping the environment safe (HE-01), following mealtime and diet instructions (FD-01) and giving medications only as permitted by HC-01 and HC-02.

Staff immediately report any incident, injury, change in condition, missing person or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation as required by BP-02, BP-03 and HC-04, and write the incident report before the end of the shift.

Behavior support strategies are used only as written in a plan that meets OAC 5123-2-06. Staff are trained on the plan before using it. Restrictive measures or rights restrictions are used only as allowed under BP-01 and IR-02.

Before each shift, a DSP who is impaired by alcohol or drugs must not report to work. A staff member who suspects that a colleague is impaired reports at once to the supervisor, who removes the person from duty, ensures individuals are safe and notifies the Administrator the same day.
A DSP is not assigned or paid to serve his or her own minor child or spouse. The Administrator checks for this when making assignments and at hire.
For each service billed to Medicaid, staff document the service as required by HCBS-02 and HCBS-03 and the supervisor verifies that documentation matches the ISP.

For each HCBS delivered (Homemaker/Personal Care or Shared Living), the Administrator confirms that the service is authorized in the ISP and that the service follows the rule that applies to it, as set out in HCBS-01.

The supervisor checks at least monthly that services were delivered as the ISP directs, notes any missed or changed services and the reason, and informs the SSA when the ISP cannot be implemented as written.
The Administrator reviews incidents, documentation and ISP implementation findings through the internal compliance and monitoring processes (IC-01 and MP-02) and corrects any gaps.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures services follow ISPs and applicable rules, assigns staff appropriately and acts on monitoring findings.
Briefs staff, verifies ISP implementation and documentation, removes impaired staff from duty and follows up on incidents.
Reads the ISP, delivers person-centered services, prevents incidents, reports and documents.
Develops and monitors the ISP and is notified when it cannot be carried out as written.

documentation: Signed ISP acknowledgments
Shift briefing and communication log
Service documentation and daily notes
Incident reports
Behavior support plans and staff training on them
Monthly ISP implementation review notes
Record of removal from duty for impairment, if any

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Background Investigations for Employment
policies.applies_to: All applicants and employees of [AGENCY NAME], including the administrator, natural-person licensee or operator, supervisors of DSPs, DSPs, direct support assistants and volunteers, and anyone under contract who has direct access to individuals
policies.purpose: To make sure no person is employed in a position with access to individuals unless a complete background investigation has been done and the person is eligible under OAC 5123-2-02.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b)(vii) — Background investigations for employment in accordance with rule 5123-2-02 of the Administrative Code. Before hire, [AGENCY NAME] obtains an application, attempts references, and checks the seven required databases: the Office of Inspector General (OIG) exclusion list, the DODD abuser registry, the nurse aide registry, the sex offender registry, the System for Award Management (SAM), the Ohio Department of Medicaid (ODM) exclusion list and the Department of Rehabilitation and Correction (DRC) offender search. A person listed in any category in OAC 5123-2-02(C)(2)(a)-(f) is not hired. [AGENCY NAME] requests a BCII criminal records check, and an FBI check if the person has not been an Ohio resident for the past five years. Conditional employment is limited to 60 days. The administrator, and a natural-person licensee or operator, must consent to Rapback under OAC 5123-3-01(D)(1). DSPs are enrolled in Rapback within 14 days and databases are rechecked at least every five years.

definitions.definition: The Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation criminal records check.
A continuous criminal history monitoring service that notifies the agency of new arrests or convictions for enrolled persons.
Limited employment allowed under OAC 5123-2-02 while a criminal records check result is pending, for no more than 60 days.
OIG exclusion list, abuser registry, nurse aide registry, sex offender registry, SAM, ODM exclusion list and DRC offender search.
A signed agreement by the employee to tell [AGENCY NAME] within 14 days if he or she is charged with, or convicted of, any offense that would disqualify the person from employment.

procedures: Before any offer of employment, the Administrator or HR designee ([HR DESIGNEE NAME]) obtains a completed application from the applicant, including employment history and a statement of any criminal history.
The HR designee attempts to contact references or prior employers, and records the date, person contacted and result of each attempt, including unsuccessful attempts.

Before hire, the HR designee checks all seven databases (OIG, abuser registry, nurse aide registry, sex offender registry, SAM, ODM exclusion list and DRC offender search), prints or saves the result of each search with the date and the name of the person who performed it.
If the applicant appears on a list or has a record described in OAC 5123-2-02(C)(2)(a)-(f), the Administrator does not hire the person and documents the reason in a confidential file.
The applicant signs a written attestation under OAC 5123-2-02 and a 14-day charge-notice agreement before starting work. Both are placed in the personnel file.
For any person who will drive individuals, the HR designee obtains a driving record before the person drives and reviews it against the criteria in TR-01.

The HR designee requests a BCII criminal records check for each applicant. If the applicant has not lived in Ohio for the past five years, the HR designee also requests an FBI check. The date of the request is recorded.

Conditional employment is permitted only as OAC 5123-2-02 allows, and for no more than 60 days. The HR designee calendars the 60th day, and if the results have not been received, the person is terminated on day 61 and may not work with individuals.

A conditionally employed person is not left alone with individuals and does not provide care unsupervised until the criminal records check result and all other pre-hire requirements are complete and eligible.
The administrator and any natural-person licensee or operator sign the Rapback consent. The HR designee enrolls each DSP in Rapback within 14 days of hire and records the enrollment date.

The HR designee reruns the seven database checks for every employee at least every five years, and sooner when [AGENCY NAME] has reason to question eligibility. The recheck dates are tracked on a master tracking list.

The HR designee applies the same pre-hire and ongoing requirements to supervisors, direct support assistants (age 16-17) and volunteers, as set out in DV-01 and DV-02, and to every other person for whom OAC 5123-2-02 applies.

When Rapback or a database recheck shows a new record, the Administrator reviews it the same day, removes the person from duty with individuals if eligibility is in question and acts as OAC 5123-2-02 requires, including terminating employment where the person is no longer eligible.
When an employee reports a charge under the 14-day agreement, the Administrator reviews it the same day, decides about the employee's duties and documents the action taken.
Each January, the Administrator gives each employee the annual written notice of conduct leading to abuser registry placement and of the 14-day charge-reporting duty, as described in ST-01.
The compliance officer verifies background investigation files quarterly under IC-01, and the results are reported to the governing board.

responsibilities.duty: Makes final hiring decisions only after all background requirements are met, and acts on new findings.
Runs and documents database checks, requests BCII and FBI checks, manages conditional employment dates, Rapback enrollment and five-year rechecks.
Gives accurate information, signs the attestation and the charge-notice agreement and reports charges within 14 days.
Audits background investigation files and reports results.
Receives audit results through the internal compliance program.

documentation: Application and reference contact log
Dated results of the seven database checks
BCII and FBI check requests and results
Signed attestation and 14-day charge-notice agreement
Driving record for drivers
Conditional employment start date and 60-day calendar
Rapback consent and enrollment confirmations
Five-year recheck tracking list
Record of any non-hire decision (confidential)

policies.title: Internal Compliance Program: Chapter 5123-3, Background Investigations, Service Delivery and Billing
policies.applies_to: The governing board, Administrator, compliance officer, supervisors, DSPs, billing staff and all personnel who create records or submit claims
policies.purpose: To prevent, find and correct violations of residential facility rules, background investigation requirements and service delivery, documentation and billing rules, and to prevent improper Medicaid claims.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an established internal compliance program, as required by OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c). This policy meets: OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c)(i) — Residential facilities in accordance with rules in Chapter 5123-3 of the Administrative Code; OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c)(ii) — Background investigations and appropriate actions in accordance with rule 5123-2-02 for the administrator, licensee, operator, supervisors of DSPs, DSPs, direct support assistants and volunteers; and OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c)(iii) — Service delivery, service documentation and billing for services in accordance with Chapter 5123 of the Revised Code and rules adopted pursuant to that chapter for supported living services and the specific home and community-based services provided. [AGENCY NAME] audits itself on a set schedule, reconciles service documentation, schedules and electronic visit verification (EVV) against billing before each claim is submitted, and reports audit findings to the governing board. Management of individuals' funds is also part of this program (IC-02). [AGENCY NAME] takes part in DODD data collection when asked. This policy supports compliance with the federal rules on Medicaid payments (42 USC 1396b(l)).

definitions.definition: The set of written procedures, audits, training, reporting and corrective actions [AGENCY NAME] uses to make sure it follows the rules.
An electronic record of the date, time, place, service and worker for each Homemaker/Personal Care visit billed in 15-minute units.
Matching each claim line to the ISP, authorization, signed service documentation, staff schedule and EVV record before the claim is submitted.
The person designated by the Administrator to run the internal compliance program, [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME].
Any Medicaid payment received that [AGENCY NAME] was not entitled to, for any reason.

procedures: The governing board adopts this policy, and the Administrator designates a compliance officer who has access to the board. The compliance officer's name and contact information are shared with all staff.

The compliance officer keeps an annual audit calendar, approved by the Administrator, that schedules the Chapter 5123-3 audit, the background investigation audit and the service documentation and billing audit.

Chapter 5123-3 audit (C(5)(c)(i)): at least annually the compliance officer audits the facility against each requirement in Chapter 5123-3 using a checklist, including license posting, policies, staffing, training, drills, medication, records, environment, individuals' rights and reports. Findings are recorded.

Background investigation audit (C(5)(c)(ii)): at least quarterly the compliance officer reviews the personnel file of every administrator, licensee, operator, supervisor, DSP, direct support assistant and volunteer to verify the database checks, BCII/FBI results, attestation, charge-notice agreement, driving record, Rapback enrollment and five-year recheck dates required by OAC 5123-2-02 (see MP-05).

If an audit finds a person without a complete background investigation, the Administrator removes the person from direct contact with individuals that day, completes the missing step and documents the appropriate action under OAC 5123-2-02.

Service delivery audit (C(5)(c)(iii)): at least monthly the compliance officer or supervisor reviews a sample of each service's documentation for the elements required by OAC 5123-9-30(E): service type, date, place, individual's name and Medicaid ID, provider and contract number, signature or initials, group size, description tied to the ISP, units or time, and start and stop times.

For Homemaker/Personal Care, the compliance officer verifies each service was delivered under an ISP, that the person does not also receive shared living or money management services from [AGENCY NAME] in the same period, that approved substitute coverage was used when the regular DSP was absent, and that EVV was used for 15-minute units.
For Shared Living, the compliance officer verifies the service follows the Chapter 5123-9 rule and HCBS-01, including the documented setting and capacity limits.

Billing staff do not submit any claim until the claim is reconciled to the ISP and authorization, signed service documentation, the staff schedule and the EVV record. Any claim line that cannot be supported is held and not billed.
Billing staff submit claims within the time limit set by DODD and ODM (currently within 350 days of the date of service for HPC) and keep a log of claim submission dates.
The compliance officer reviews overtime for each DSP using the documented overtime review process required for HPC (see PS-02). Overtime that is not supported by an ISP-based need is corrected.

If an error or overpayment is found, the compliance officer notifies the Administrator within 5 business days, the claim is corrected or the overpayment is repaid by the process required by DODD or ODM, and the cause is fixed. The correction is logged.

Staff are trained on compliance at orientation and annually, including how to document services and how to report a compliance concern without retaliation. Concerns may be reported to the compliance officer or Administrator, or directly to the governing board chair.

The compliance officer prepares a written report of all audit findings, corrective actions and their completion dates each quarter and gives it to the governing board, which reviews it and records its review in the minutes (see MP-02 and GOV-01).
When DODD requests data or participation in data collection, the Administrator responds as set out in MP-02 and keeps a record of the response.
The compliance officer follows up on each correction within 30 days to verify it is in place, and reviews and updates this program at least annually.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts and monitors the internal compliance program and reviews quarterly audit reports.
Resources and supports the program, removes ineligible staff from duty and ensures corrections are made.
Runs the audit calendar, reconciles records, tracks corrections and reports to the board.
Do not submit unsupported claims, keep claim records and correct errors.
Create accurate, timely service documentation and use EVV as required.

documentation: Annual audit calendar
Chapter 5123-3 audit checklists
Quarterly background investigation audit results
Monthly service documentation review samples
Billing reconciliation worksheets (ISP, documentation, schedule, EVV, claim)
Claim submission log
Overtime review records
Corrective action and overpayment repayment log
Quarterly reports to the governing board and board minutes

policies.title: Management of Individuals' Funds
policies.applies_to: All employees, supervisors, the Administrator and the operator of [AGENCY NAME] who handle, hold, account for or advise on funds or negotiable property of individuals living in the DODD-licensed residential facility at [ADDRESS].
policies.purpose: To make sure each individual manages his or her own money to the extent of the individual's ability, that any funds [AGENCY NAME] holds or helps manage are protected, tracked and reconciled, and that funds management is reviewed as part of the internal compliance program.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c)(iv) — Management of individuals' funds (checklist item C(5)(c)(iv)). Under ORC 5123.62 (C47), individuals have the right to manage their own finances to the extent of their ability. [AGENCY NAME] will not take control of an individual's money except as the individual (or the individual's legal guardian) authorizes in writing and as the ISP provides. Where [AGENCY NAME] holds or assists with funds, it will keep a separate account transaction record for each individual and reconcile it, as referenced in OAC 5123-3-04(J)(1)(b)(vii) and OAC 5123-2-07. It will also keep a record of negotiable items the individual owns. At termination of residency, [AGENCY NAME] will account for the individual's personal funds and release or dispose of them as directed, in a written accounting delivered within 30 days. Management of individuals' funds is a standing review area of the internal compliance program (OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(c); C10). The funds of one individual are never used for another individual, for staff, or for the operation of the facility.

definitions.definition: Cash, checking or savings balances, benefit payments (such as SSI or wages), prepaid cards, and any other money belonging to an individual, whether held by the individual or by [AGENCY NAME] for the individual.
Items that can be converted to cash or used to obtain money or goods, such as checks, money orders, gift cards, savings bonds, stock certificates and ATM or debit cards, owned by the individual.
A running ledger for one individual showing each deposit and withdrawal, with date, amount, purpose, balance, receipt reference and signatures.
A comparison of the transaction record to cash on hand, bank statements and receipts to confirm that balances match and every entry is supported.

procedures: At admission and at least annually at the ISP meeting, the Administrator (or designee) works with the individual, the guardian if any, and the service and support administrator to assess how much of his or her own money the individual can manage, and records the result in the ISP or service record.

Individuals who can manage their money keep control of it. Staff may offer teaching or support (for example, budgeting or bank visits) only as the ISP states, and staff never take possession without written authorization.

If an individual or guardian asks [AGENCY NAME] to hold or help manage funds, the Administrator obtains a signed, dated written authorization that states what [AGENCY NAME] will do, the limits, and how the individual may get his or her money on request.

[AGENCY NAME] holds funds only in a way that is separate from agency operating funds. Funds of individuals are never commingled with agency money, with staff money or with other individuals' money. Each individual has a separate account or a separately identified sub-account.
Cash held on site is kept in a locked container, with access limited to the Administrator and designated staff named in writing.

For each individual whose funds are held or managed, staff open an account transaction record. Every deposit and withdrawal is entered the day it occurs, with the date, amount, purpose, running balance, and the signature of the staff member. The individual also signs, or the entry states why not.

A receipt or other proof is attached or referenced for every expenditure. Purchases are made for the individual's own benefit and choice. Staff may not borrow from, lend to, or accept gifts or payment from an individual.

Staff keep a separate list of negotiable items the individual owns, with a description, identifying number, date received, and date and reason for any change in status. Entries are signed by two staff members when practicable.

Staff reconcile each account transaction record at least monthly against cash on hand, bank statements and receipts. Someone other than the staff member who made the entries performs or reviews the reconciliation, and both sign and date it.

Any discrepancy is reported to the Administrator the same day it is found. The Administrator investigates, corrects with a documented entry (never by erasing), and restores any missing funds. Suspected theft, misuse or exploitation is handled and reported under BP-02 and BP-03.

If [AGENCY NAME] or an employee is appointed representative payee for an individual's benefits, the Administrator follows the paying agency's rules in addition to this policy. [AGENCY NAME] will keep the individual's benefit funds separate and will not use them to pay fees the individual has not agreed to.
Individuals or their guardians may review their account transaction record and negotiable items list on request, in a timely way, and receive a copy.

At least quarterly, the Administrator performs an internal compliance review of funds management. The review samples each individual's transaction record, reconciliations, authorizations and receipts, and the result is recorded in the internal compliance log (see IC-01).
The operator reviews the quarterly results and requires corrective action, retraining or personnel action for any finding.

When an individual's residency ends for any reason, the Administrator reconciles the account, prepares a written accounting of all personal funds and negotiable items, and delivers it within 30 days to the individual or guardian (and to the receiving provider, when applicable).

Funds and negotiable items are released, transferred or disposed of as the individual or guardian directs in writing, and the recipient signs for them. The signed receipt and accounting are filed in the service record. In the event of an individual's death, the Administrator follows HC-05 and applicable law for release to the lawful representative.
Records are retained as required under RC-03.

responsibilities.duty: Approves this policy, reviews quarterly funds-management results and ensures corrective action.

Assesses ability to manage funds, secures written authorizations, oversees accounts, performs or assigns reconciliation, conducts the quarterly internal review and prepares the 30-day termination accounting.
Support individuals' own money management as the ISP directs, record every transaction accurately, keep receipts and report discrepancies immediately.
Decides how much help is wanted, signs authorizations and may review records at any time.

documentation: Funds-management assessment in the ISP or service record
Signed written authorization to hold or manage funds
Account transaction record for each individual
Receipts and bank statements
Negotiable items record
Monthly reconciliation sign-offs
Discrepancy and corrective-action reports
Quarterly internal compliance review records
Written termination accounting and signed receipt for release of funds

policies.title: Safeguarding Individuals' Rights (ORC 5123.62-5123.65)
policies.applies_to: The operator, Administrator, supervisors, direct support professionals, support staff, direct support assistants and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME], in the residential facility at [ADDRESS] and in all HCBS settings.
policies.purpose: To make sure the operator and every employee interact with individuals in ways that safeguard their rights under ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65, and that [AGENCY NAME] meets the requirements of ORC 5123.63 and 5123.64.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(e) (checklist item C(5)(e)) — ensuring the operator and its employees interact with individuals in a way that safeguards the rights enumerated in ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65 — and OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(f) (checklist item C(5)(f)) — meeting the requirements established under ORC 5123.63 and 5123.64. Rights under ORC 5123.62 (C47) include: dignity and respect; privacy; free communication; personal possessions; managing finances to the extent of ability; confidentiality of records; the right to file grievances without reprisal; freedom from unnecessary restraint; living free from abuse; access to medical care; and voting. [AGENCY NAME] will honor those rights in daily practice. Any limit on a right is permitted only through the due process in IR-02. Grievances are accepted and resolved without reprisal. Rights are covered in orientation and in annual training for all staff. For HCBS settings, [AGENCY NAME] also follows the federal home and community-based settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) (see IR-01). The Administrator will keep the current text of ORC 5123.62 through 5123.65 on file, confirm the specific duties in ORC 5123.63 and 5123.64 against that text at least annually, and map each to a procedure below.

definitions.definition: The rights of persons with a developmental disability enumerated in ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65, together with the duties established under ORC 5123.63 and 5123.64.
Any retaliation, threat, discouragement or negative treatment because an individual, family member, guardian, advocate or employee asserted a right or made a complaint.
Any limit placed on an individual's exercise of a right, which is allowed only through the process in IR-02.

procedures: The Administrator keeps on file the current text of ORC 5123.62, 5123.63, 5123.64 and 5123.65 and, at least annually and whenever the law changes, reviews it and updates a rights crosswalk that ties each statutory duty to the procedure and record that meets it.

Before or at admission, the Administrator gives each individual (and guardian) a written statement of rights in plain language or the individual's preferred format, explains it in a way he or she understands, and records the explanation and the individual's acknowledgment in the service record.

The rights statement and the grievance procedure (IR-03) are posted in a common area of the facility where individuals can see them, and the Administrator confirms the posting during monthly walk-throughs.

Every new employee, volunteer and direct support assistant receives rights training during orientation before working alone with individuals. The training covers each right in ORC 5123.62, how it applies in daily routines, and how to report a concern. The written training plan (ST-04) lists the topic and competency method.
Every employee repeats rights training at least annually. Training is recorded in the training record with the description, date, duration and instructor.

Staff honor privacy and dignity: they knock and wait before entering bedrooms and bathrooms, provide personal care in private, speak respectfully, and do not discuss an individual's personal matters in front of others.
Staff protect free communication: individuals may send and receive mail unopened, use the telephone and electronic communication privately, and have visitors as the ISP and IR-01 provide.
Individuals keep and use their own possessions (CL-01), and manage their own money to the extent of their ability (IC-02, IR-04).

Individuals decide on their own medical care to the extent of their ability, and staff arrange access to medical, dental and other health care as needed (HC-04). Staff support registration and voting for any individual who chooses it.
Restraint, seclusion and other restrictive measures are used only as allowed by BP-01 and IR-02. Staff never use restraint as punishment, for staff convenience or in place of programming.

Any limit on a right (for example, a restriction on food access, visitors or money) must have a documented specific assessed need, a plan, informed consent and periodic review under IR-02. A staff member may not impose a limit on his or her own authority.
Staff report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately under BP-02 and BP-03.

Individuals, guardians, family and staff may raise a concern orally or in writing to any staff member or the Administrator. The concern is logged and handled under IR-03. No one is threatened, disciplined, moved, or treated differently because of a complaint, and any suspected reprisal is investigated by the operator or a person outside the chain of the person accused.
Supervisors observe staff interactions at least monthly and record any rights concern. Concerns result in coaching, retraining or personnel action documented in the personnel record.

As part of the internal compliance program (IC-01), the Administrator reviews rights practices at least quarterly: posted notices, acknowledgments, restrictions, grievances and incident reports. The operator reviews the results and orders corrective action.
Rights information, restrictions and grievance results are shared with the DODD, county board or other regulator on request and during compliance reviews (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resources, training and corrective action so that rights are safeguarded; reviews quarterly rights results.
Maintains the statutory crosswalk, provides rights statements and postings, schedules training and conducts the quarterly review.
Observe interactions, correct violations, and report concerns to the Administrator.
Treat individuals in ways that safeguard their rights, complete training, and report violations and suspected abuse without delay.
Are informed of rights, may exercise them and may file grievances without reprisal.

documentation: Current text of ORC 5123.62-5123.65 and the annual rights crosswalk
Signed rights acknowledgments in service records
Photo or log of posted rights statement and grievance procedure
Orientation and annual rights training records
Supervisor observation notes
Rights restriction documentation (IR-02)
Grievance log and resolutions
Quarterly internal compliance review of rights

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: Annual Staff Notice: Abuser Registry Conduct and 14-Day Charge Reporting
policies.applies_to: All supervisors, direct support professionals, direct support assistants and other employees of [AGENCY NAME], and the Administrator and operator who administer notices.
policies.purpose: To give every staff member written notice each year of the conduct that can lead to placement on the abuser registry and of the duty to report charges within 14 days, and to set the conduct limits for direct support professionals listed on the state checklist.
policies.policy: This policy meets checklist item D(2) (as listed: OAC 5123-3-04(D)(2)), the limits on direct support professionals, and implements the annual written notice required by OAC 5123-3-01(D)(1)-(2) (C12). [AGENCY NAME] will ensure that a direct support professional does not: (a) provide services to the DSP's minor child; (b) provide services to the DSP's spouse; (c) provide services to the minor child of the Administrator; (d) provide services to the spouse of the Administrator; (e) administer medication or perform health-related activities unless the DSP meets the applicable requirements of Chapters 4723., 5123. and 5126. of the Revised Code; or (f) use or be under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs, illegal chemical substances or controlled substances that may adversely affect the ability to furnish services while providing services. Each year, [AGENCY NAME] gives every staff member written notice of the conduct that can lead to placement on the abuser registry and of the duty of supervisors, DSPs and direct support assistants to report in writing to the operator, within 14 calendar days, a formal charge, conviction, guilty plea or finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for any offense listed in ORC 109.572(A)(3)(a)-(e). A signed acknowledgment is kept in the personnel file.

definitions.definition: The state registry maintained by DODD of persons found to have committed abuse, neglect, misappropriation or exploitation of individuals with developmental disabilities; placement bars employment in these positions.

A written report to the operator, within 14 calendar days, of a formal charge, conviction, guilty plea or finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for an offense listed in ORC 109.572(A)(3)(a)-(e).
A court program in which a case is stayed or dismissed on completion of treatment or conditions; a finding of eligibility must be reported.

procedures: The Administrator maintains one written Annual Staff Notice that (1) describes conduct that can lead to abuser registry placement, such as abuse, neglect, misappropriation of property, exploitation and failure to report, in plain language; (2) explains the 14-day written reporting duty and the offenses in ORC 109.572(A)(3)(a)-(e); and (3) lists the DSP limits in items D(2)(a) through (f).

The Administrator gives the notice to each new employee on or before the first day of work, and to every staff member at least once every 12 months (set date: [MONTH]) thereafter. The Administrator keeps a master list of staff and delivery dates.

The employee reads the notice, has the chance to ask questions, and signs and dates an acknowledgment. The signed acknowledgment is filed in the personnel file (ST-03). Staff who have not signed within 7 days are not scheduled until the notice is signed.

Staff who report a charge, conviction, guilty plea or finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction do so in writing to the operator (or Administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], who passes it to the operator) within 14 calendar days of the event. The notice states the date, court, offense and status.
The person receiving a report date-stamps it, gives the employee a copy, and immediately notifies the operator if the recipient is not the operator.

Within 2 business days of receiving a report, the operator reviews it against the disqualifying offenses and standards in MP-05, decides whether the employee may continue working, work with restrictions, or be removed from duty pending resolution, and documents the decision and reasons in a confidential file.
If the report could involve a risk to individuals, the operator removes the employee from direct care duties at once and arranges for the safety of individuals.
If the report involves abuse, neglect, misappropriation or exploitation, the operator follows BP-02 and BP-03 and the notices to DODD and others in GOV-03.

The Administrator checks each DSP's schedule at hire and at each schedule change to confirm that no DSP is assigned to provide services to the DSP's own minor child or spouse, or to the minor child or spouse of the Administrator. Any staff member whose family member is an individual served tells the Administrator in writing before assignment.

Staff may not administer medication or perform health-related activities until the Administrator verifies and records that the staff member meets the applicable requirements of Chapters 4723., 5123. and 5126. of the Revised Code (see HC-01, HC-02).

Staff may not use alcohol, illegal drugs, illegal chemical substances or controlled substances that may adversely affect their ability to furnish services while providing services. Supervisors who reasonably suspect impairment remove the employee from duty immediately, document observed behavior with a second witness when possible, and notify the Administrator.
Non-compliance results in progressive discipline up to termination, as set out in the personnel policies, and the Administrator documents the action in the personnel record.
Each year, before the notice is delivered, the Administrator reviews the notice against the current rules and ORC 109.572 and updates the text and the master list.

During quarterly internal compliance reviews (IC-01), the Administrator confirms that every active staff member has a current signed notice and that all reports received were handled within required timelines.

responsibilities.duty: Receives 14-day written reports, decides employment status, and takes protective action.
Prepares and delivers the annual notice, collects acknowledgments, schedules to avoid prohibited assignments and tracks compliance.

responsibilities.role: Supervisors, DSPs and direct support assistants
responsibilities.duty: Read and sign the notice annually, report charges and related findings in writing within 14 calendar days, and comply with the DSP limits.

documentation: Annual Staff Notice (current version and prior versions)
Signed staff acknowledgments in personnel files
Master delivery log
Written 14-day reports and operator decision records
Schedule review notes for family-member restrictions
Disciplinary records
Quarterly compliance review checklist

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: Staff Scheduling and Staff on Duty
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, supervisors, DSPs, support staff and any scheduling personnel of [AGENCY NAME] at the residential facility at [ADDRESS].
