For each record type, the Administrator identifies the applicable state and federal retention requirements. This includes confirming the Medicaid retention period in writing with ODM and DODD and the rules that apply to the facility license and the HCBS provider agreement. The source of each requirement is entered on the schedule.

The Administrator prepares the Records Retention Schedule listing each record type, the retention period (the longest applicable period), the storage location and format, the person responsible and the destruction method. The Governing Body reviews and approves the schedule and the approval is dated.

HIPAA privacy documentation, including privacy policies, training records, complaint records and dispositions, and other documentation required by 45 CFR 164.530, is kept for 6 years from the date it was created or last in effect, whichever is later. The schedule shows this period.

Records are stored in a secure, organized way that allows retrieval. Archived paper records are labeled with record type, individual and destruction-eligible date and stored in a locked location. Electronic records are backed up regularly and protected under RC-02.

Records of individuals who have left are retained for the full period on the schedule and are not destroyed early. Records involved in an open investigation, audit, appeal, claim or litigation are not destroyed until the Administrator confirms in writing that the matter is closed.
At least annually, the Administrator reviews the archive against the schedule and identifies records eligible for destruction. The Administrator approves destruction in writing.

Records are destroyed by cross-cut shredding, secure shredding service or permanent electronic deletion, and the Administrator logs the record type, date range, date and method of destruction, and the name of the person who performed or witnessed it.
The Administrator reviews the schedule at least annually and whenever a rule changes, and revises it. Revisions are approved and dated by the Governing Body.

If [AGENCY NAME] plans to transfer operation of the facility to another operator, the Administrator notifies the Governing Body and follows GOV-02 and GOV-03 for notices to DODD. The Administrator plans the conveyance of records at the same time.
On or before the transfer date, the Administrator prepares an index of the records in (J)(1) for each individual: the current records and the accessible records, as listed in RC-01.

The outgoing Administrator conveys the records to the incoming operator in a secure manner. Paper records are handed over in sealed, labeled containers and electronic records are transferred by a secure method.

The incoming operator's representative signs a receipt listing each individual's record conveyed and its date. The outgoing operator keeps a copy of the receipt and the index in agency files for the period on the retention schedule.

The outgoing operator continues to keep any agency records that are not conveyed, such as financial, billing and personnel records, for the retention period on the schedule, and protects them under RC-02.
The outgoing Administrator also coordinates the conveyance of individuals' clothing and belongings under CL-01 and of funds and medications under IC-02 and HC-03.

responsibilities.duty: Develops and maintains the retention schedule; confirms Medicaid retention periods with ODM and DODD; approves destruction; manages conveyance of records on transfer of operation.
Approves the schedule and reviews it annually; decides on and oversees any transfer of operation.
Ensures HIPAA documentation is kept for 6 years and that records are destroyed securely.
Files, stores, retrieves and logs destruction of records as directed.

documentation: Records Retention Schedule with source of each retention requirement and Governing Body approval date
Written confirmation of Medicaid retention period from ODM or DODD
Annual archive review and destruction approvals
Record destruction log
Index of records conveyed on transfer of operation
Receipt signed by the incoming operator
Notes of holds for open investigations, audits or appeals

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-05 (C)-(G) Transfer and termination of services policies
policies.title: Grounds for Transfer or Termination and Nondiscrimination
policies.applies_to: All residents of the DODD-licensed residential facility operated by [AGENCY NAME]; Administrator, Governing Body, ISP team members and all staff involved in admission, service delivery or discharge decisions
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident is allowed to remain in the facility, that a transfer or termination of services starts only for a permitted reason, and that [AGENCY NAME] never discriminates unlawfully in admission, services or discharge.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows each resident to remain in the residential facility and does not initiate a transfer or termination of services unless one of the following grounds applies, as required by OAC 5123-3-05(C)(1) (Item C(1) — Transfer and Termination Grounds): (a) the transfer or termination is necessary for the resident's welfare and the resident's needs can no longer be met without undue hardship on the operation; (b) the resident no longer needs or wants the services or chooses to move; (c) the resident is creating a significant risk of substantial harm to self, other residents or staff; (d) nonpayment for the stay, including nonpayment by Medicaid or another third-party payer; (e) the facility permanently reduces its capacity; or (f) the facility ceases to operate. [AGENCY NAME] does not unlawfully discriminate because of disability, race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex or age, including by failing to make reasonable accommodation to a person's physical, mental or behavioral support needs to the extent required by law unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship. This policy meets OAC 5123-3-05(C)(2) (Item C(2) — Nondiscrimination). [AGENCY NAME] also follows the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101 et seq.), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 USC 794) and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d). Notice, appeal and hearing steps are in TT-02 and TT-03.

definitions.definition: Moving an individual from the facility to another residential setting or provider.
Ending [AGENCY NAME]'s residential services to an individual.
A significant difficulty or expense for the operation, determined case by case on documented facts, after reasonable accommodation and available supports have been tried or considered.
A change in policy, practice, environment or support that allows a person with a disability to have equal opportunity to receive and keep services.

A documented, serious and likely danger to the individual, other residents or staff that cannot be reduced through supports, positive behavior supports, environmental changes or other reasonable measures.

procedures: The Administrator reviews this policy with every new individual and guardian at admission and explains that the person may remain in the home and that services will be ended only on the grounds in OAC 5123-3-05(C)(1). The explanation is given in a way the person understands and is noted in the record.

Before any ground for transfer or termination is considered, the Administrator calls an ISP team meeting that includes the individual, the guardian (if any), the county board service and support administrator and other team members the individual chooses. The Administrator presents the concern and the supports tried so far.

The team considers reasonable accommodations, added staffing or training, positive behavior supports (BP-01), health and nursing supports (HC-04), environmental changes and other options. The Administrator documents each option considered, its result and why it did or did not resolve the concern.
The Administrator works with the county board to try to meet the individual's needs and documents each contact, including the date, the person spoken to and what was agreed.

The Administrator may recommend a transfer or termination to the Governing Body only after confirming in writing which one of grounds (a) through (f) applies and the facts that support it. A decision based on grounds (a) or (c) requires documented evidence of the hardship or risk and of the efforts made to avoid the transfer.

For ground (b), the Administrator confirms the individual's own choice through direct conversation (with communication support as needed, see IR-01), and with the guardian when there is one. The individual's choice is documented. Staff may not pressure, coerce or encourage anyone to move.

For ground (d), the Administrator first reviews the billing and payment record, contacts the payer and the county board to resolve any payment problem, and documents those efforts. Nonpayment includes Medicaid or other third-party nonpayment.
For ground (e) or (f), the Governing Body makes the decision in writing, notifies DODD as required under GOV-03, and follows the notice requirements in TT-02 for every affected individual.

[AGENCY NAME] never initiates a transfer or termination because of a person's disability, race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex or age, or because the person filed a grievance, made a complaint, reported abuse, asserted a right or requested a hearing. A decision for any of those reasons is prohibited and is reviewed by the Governing Body.

Before admitting any person, the Administrator evaluates the person's needs without regard to a prohibited basis. The Administrator makes reasonable accommodation for physical, mental or behavioral support needs unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship, and documents the evaluation and any hardship finding.

Where a request for accommodation is denied for undue hardship, the Administrator documents the specific facts, informs the person or guardian in writing and in an understandable way, and informs them of how to file a grievance (IR-03).
The Governing Body approves each decision to initiate a transfer or termination in writing before any notice is issued. The approval states the ground, supporting facts, efforts made and the date.
After approval, the Administrator follows TT-02 for notice and TT-03 for appeal, mediation and hearing. The Administrator documents all reasons in the individual's record.

The Administrator reviews every transfer and termination at least annually with the Governing Body for patterns that suggest a need for training, staffing or program changes, and for any sign of discrimination. Results are recorded in internal monitoring (MP-02).
All staff are trained on this policy at orientation and annually, and corrective action under PS-01 applies to any violation.

responsibilities.duty: Approves every decision to start a transfer or termination; ensures no decision is based on a prohibited reason; reviews transfer and termination activity annually.
Convenes the team; documents efforts and accommodations; confirms the ground; coordinates with the county board; ensures nondiscrimination in admission and services.

responsibilities.role: ISP Team / County Board service and support administrator
responsibilities.duty: Helps problem-solve and plan alternatives and supports the individual's choices.
Provides accurate, factual documentation of events; reports concerns promptly; does not discourage anyone from remaining in the home.

documentation: Team meeting notes on concerns, options considered and accommodations tried
Contacts with the county board, including dates and outcomes
Written statement of the ground relied on and supporting facts
Documentation of the individual's choice, where ground (b) applies
Billing and payer contact records, where ground (d) applies
Accommodation requests and responses, including any undue hardship finding
Governing Body approval
Annual transfer and termination review

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-05 (C)-(G) Transfer and termination of services policies
policies.title: Notice of Transfer or Termination
policies.applies_to: All residents of the DODD-licensed residential facility operated by [AGENCY NAME]; Administrator, Governing Body, ISP team and staff involved in transfer or termination
policies.purpose: To make sure that before any transfer or termination of services, the individual and the county board receive complete written notice by certified mail, the notice and appeal rights are explained in a way the person understands, the required notice period is met, and services continue during an appeal unless an emergency exists or the person waives appeal rights.
policies.policy: Before initiating a transfer or termination of services, [AGENCY NAME] (a) notifies the individual and the county board in writing by certified mail, with a notice containing (i) the reason, (ii) the effective date, (iii) a summary of the action [AGENCY NAME] has taken, including working with the county board, to try to meet the resident's needs, (iv) the individual's right to appeal and the appeal process, and (v) the telephone number and address of Disability Rights Ohio; (b) explains the transfer or termination and the appeal rights in a manner the individual understands; and (c) records the reasons in the resident's record. This policy meets OAC 5123-3-05(C)(3) (Item C(3) — Notice Content and Explanation). Notice is made at least 30 calendar days before the transfer or termination, except when an emergency exists; if the emergency conditions no longer exist before the 30 days expire, the individual may return. If the individual requests a hearing, [AGENCY NAME] maintains services or the availability of services until a decision is rendered, unless an emergency exists. If the individual waives appeal rights in writing, [AGENCY NAME] is not required to maintain services. This policy meets OAC 5123-3-05(C)(4)-(6) (Item C(4)-(6) — 30-Day Notice, Emergencies, Services During Hearing and Waiver). A notice is issued only after a ground has been confirmed under TT-01. Appeal, mediation and hearing procedures are in TT-03.

definitions.definition: United States Postal Service certified mail, with proof of mailing and a return receipt or tracking record.
The date the transfer or termination takes effect, no earlier than 30 calendar days after the notice is given, except in an emergency.

A situation in which delay would place the individual, other residents or staff at immediate risk of serious harm, or in which the facility can no longer safely operate, as documented by the Administrator.
Ohio's protection and advocacy organization for people with disabilities, whose telephone number and address must appear in the notice.
A written statement signed by the individual (or guardian where applicable) giving up the right to appeal the transfer or termination.

procedures: Before preparing a notice, the Administrator confirms that the Governing Body has approved the transfer or termination under TT-01 and that one of the permitted grounds is documented.

The Administrator prepares the written notice using the agency's Notice of Transfer or Termination form in plain language. The notice states: (i) the reason; (ii) the effective date; (iii) a summary of actions taken, including work with the county board, to try to meet the person's needs; (iv) the individual's right to appeal and how to appeal; and (v) the telephone number and address of Disability Rights Ohio.
The Administrator checks that the effective date is at least 30 calendar days after the date of mailing, unless an emergency exists, and counts the days on the file copy.

The Administrator sends the notice to the individual by certified mail, and to the guardian where there is one, and to the county board by certified mail on the same day. The Administrator keeps the certified mail receipt, tracking record and return receipt, and also hand-delivers a copy to the individual and documents the delivery.

Within the same week the notice is mailed, and before it takes effect, the Administrator meets with the individual (and guardian, if any) to explain the transfer or termination, the reasons, the effective date and the appeal rights in a way the person understands. The Administrator uses the person's usual communication method, plain language, translation, interpretation or assistive communication as needed (IR-01), and may ask a trusted person or advocate to attend.

The Administrator records in the individual's record the reasons for the transfer or termination, the date of mailing, the date and manner of the explanation, who was present and how the individual responded.

The Administrator works with the individual, guardian and county board to plan the move, including identifying a new setting, visits, transportation, transfer of records, medications, funds and belongings, and continuity of health care. Planning steps are documented.

If the individual or guardian asks for an appeal or hearing, the Administrator immediately records the date and manner of the request, forwards it as required under TT-03, and continues services or the availability of services until a decision is rendered, unless an emergency exists.

If an emergency exists, the Administrator documents the facts of the emergency, notifies the individual, guardian and county board in writing as soon as possible with the same content required in the notice, and takes the steps needed to protect health and safety. The Administrator reports any required incident under BP-03.

If an emergency ends before the 30 days expire, the Administrator tells the individual in writing that the person may return, and arranges the return promptly where the facility can safely serve the person. The decision and communication are recorded.

If the individual wishes to waive appeal rights, the Administrator first explains again what the waiver means and that it is voluntary. The waiver is made in writing, signed and dated by the individual (or guardian where applicable), and filed in the record. [AGENCY NAME] never asks for or pressures a waiver as a condition of any service or benefit.

On or before the transfer or termination date, the Administrator coordinates with the receiving provider and county board on records, identification, prescriptions and medications (HC-03), personal funds (IC-02, IR-04), and clothing and belongings (CL-01). Items are conveyed with signed receipts where possible.

Within 30 calendar days after the residency ends, the Administrator completes the written accounting required by RC-01: the circumstances of termination, the new address, conveyance of records, identification, prescriptions and medications, disposition of clothing and belongings, and release or disposition of personal funds. The accounting is signed, dated and filed.

The Administrator files copies of the notice, certified mail receipts, county board contacts, explanation notes, any waiver, hearing request and the accounting in the individual's record, and tracks them on a transfer and termination log.
The Administrator reports each completed transfer or termination to the Governing Body and reports to DODD where required under GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and sends notices by certified mail to the individual and county board; ensures at least 30 days' notice; explains the notice and appeal rights; maintains services during a hearing; completes the 30-day accounting.
Approves the decision before notice is issued and receives reports on each transfer and termination.
Continues providing services during the notice period and any appeal; supports the individual emotionally and practically through the move; assists with packing and inventories.

responsibilities.role: County Board service and support administrator
responsibilities.duty: Receives the notice, works with [AGENCY NAME] on alternatives and assists with finding a new setting.
May appeal, request a hearing, waive appeal rights in writing, or return if an emergency ends within the notice period.

documentation: Notice of Transfer or Termination with the content required by OAC 5123-3-05(C)(3)
Certified mail receipts, tracking records and return receipts for the individual (and guardian) and the county board
Record of explanation to the individual, including date, method and persons present
Reasons recorded in the individual's record
County board contact log and move plan
Hearing request record, where applicable
Written waiver of appeal rights, where applicable
Emergency documentation, where applicable
Written accounting completed within 30 calendar days after residency ends
Transfer and termination log

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-05 (C)-(G) Transfer and termination of services policies
policies.title: Appeal, Mediation and Hearing Process
policies.applies_to: DODD-licensed residential facility: all individuals who receive a notice of transfer or termination, their guardians and advocates, the administrator, the governing board and all staff who handle notices or appeals
policies.purpose: To give every individual who receives a notice of transfer or termination a fair, timely and clearly explained way to challenge it. The process runs from an administrative review through DODD mediation to a hearing, and [AGENCY NAME] follows each deadline and the director's final decision.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will honor every individual's right to appeal a notice of transfer or termination. This policy meets OAC 5123-3-05(D)(1)-(3) (administrative review), OAC 5123-3-05(E) (mediation), OAC 5123-3-05(F) (hearing) and OAC 5123-3-05(G) (consequences of non-compliance).

Item D(1)-(3), Administrative review: The individual first appeals in writing to the governing board or the administrator within seven calendar days of receiving the notice. The governing board or administrator notifies the individual in writing of the outcome within five calendar days. The response is sent by certified mail. If the appeal is denied, the response includes an explanation and the contact information for the DODD director. The individual then has five calendar days from receipt of that response to appeal in writing to the director.

Item E(1)-(6), Mediation: Before any hearing, the individual and [AGENCY NAME] will attend a mediation meeting. Legal representation is not permitted at mediation. DODD provides the mediator. The meeting is held within fifteen calendar days of receipt of the appeal. Mediation is nonbinding unless all parties agree in writing. Statements made in mediation cannot be used as evidence in later hearings or court proceedings, and [AGENCY NAME] will not offer or rely on them for that purpose.

Item F(1)-(10), Hearing: DODD grants a hearing to an individual who received a notice, attended mediation and requests a hearing. DODD appoints the hearing officer, who is not the mediator. The hearing is held within thirty calendar days of the end of mediation. The burden of proof is on [AGENCY NAME] as operator. The hearing officer issues a written recommendation within ten calendar days. The director issues a written decision within five calendar days and may impose conditions. [AGENCY NAME] will comply with the decision and every condition.

Item G, Non-compliance: If [AGENCY NAME] fails to follow this rule or the director's decision, it may be subject to adverse action under OAC 5123-3-06. That can include suspension of admissions, a monitor, or refusal to renew or revocation of the license. The agency treats compliance with these steps as a licensure obligation.

No staff member may discourage, delay or retaliate against an individual for appealing. Individuals are told they may be supported by a guardian, family member, advocate or other person of their choosing.

definitions.definition: The licensee, or the entity contracted by the licensee, that runs the residential facility and issued the notice of transfer or termination.
The written notice of transfer or termination given under TT-02.
The first-level appeal to the governing board or administrator.
A nonbinding meeting led by a DODD-provided mediator, held before any hearing.
The person appointed by DODD to hear the case. This person is never the mediator.
Every day, including weekends and holidays. The deadlines in this policy are counted in calendar days.

procedures: When a notice is issued under TT-02, the administrator confirms that it includes a plain-language explanation of the right to appeal, the seven-calendar-day deadline, and the name, address and phone number of the person to whom the appeal is sent ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [ADDRESS], [PHONE]). The notice is also offered in the individual's preferred language or format (see IR-01).

On the day the notice is delivered, the administrator records the delivery date and method on the Appeal Tracking Log. The log has columns for notice date, receipt date, appeal due date, response due date, mediation date, hearing date, recommendation date and decision date.

The administrator or designee explains the appeal steps verbally to the individual and guardian. They also offer help writing the appeal, such as scribing the individual's words if requested, and give contact information for advocacy supports. This is documented in the service record.

Staff who receive an appeal in any form (letter, email, or a spoken request for help appealing) give it to the administrator the same day. The administrator date-stamps it and enters the receipt date in the log. Staff do not screen, refuse or discourage an appeal.

Within one business day of receiving the appeal, the administrator gives the governing board chair ([GOVERNING BOARD CHAIR]) a copy of the notice, the appeal and the supporting records. The administrator then schedules the board or administrator review so a decision can be made well inside five calendar days.

The reviewer (the board or the administrator, as the governing document provides) considers the appeal, the stated grounds for transfer or termination, the individual's service record, and any person-centered plan information. The reviewer must not have been the person who made the original decision where another reviewer is available. The reasons for the outcome are recorded in writing.

Within five calendar days of receiving the appeal, the administrator sends the written outcome to the individual and guardian by certified mail. If the appeal is denied, the letter includes an explanation of the reasons and the DODD director's contact information, and says that the individual has five calendar days from receipt to appeal in writing to the director. The administrator keeps the certified mail receipt and return receipt with the log.

If the individual appeals to the director, the administrator cooperates fully with DODD requests, supplies records on time, and tells the individual and guardian whom to contact at DODD. The administrator records the date DODD notifies the agency of the director-level appeal.

After DODD schedules mediation (to be held within fifteen calendar days of receipt of the appeal), the administrator confirms the date, time and place with DODD. The administrator also checks that the individual can attend, with accessible transportation, an interpreter, a communication device or an advocate as needed, and arranges those supports at no cost to the individual.

Before mediation, the administrator reviews the case with the board chair. [AGENCY NAME] sends a representative with authority to resolve the matter (the administrator or a designee). The representative does not bring an attorney, because legal representation is not permitted at mediation, and the agency tells the individual that the same limit applies to them.

At mediation, agency representatives participate in good faith, listen to the individual's concerns and consider options such as added supports, changes to the plan, or a more suitable placement. Any agreement is binding only if every party agrees in writing. The administrator keeps a copy of any signed agreement and makes sure it is carried out.

No agency staff member will offer, quote or place in a hearing file any statement made during mediation, and mediation statements are not kept in the individual's service record. Only the signed agreement (if any) and the fact that mediation occurred and its date are recorded.

If mediation does not resolve the matter and the individual requests a hearing, the administrator confirms with DODD that the hearing will be held within thirty calendar days of the end of mediation. The administrator then assembles the notice, the service record, incident and behavior documentation, and the evidence supporting the transfer or termination.

[AGENCY NAME] recognizes that the burden of proof at the hearing is on the operator. The administrator and board chair verify that every factual claim in the notice is supported by dated documentation and that the grounds meet TT-01. If the evidence is not sufficient, the board considers withdrawing the notice.

At the hearing, the administrator and any witnesses attend, answer the hearing officer's questions and present records. Staff witnesses are prepared in advance and told to be truthful and factual. The agency makes sure the individual is not subjected to retaliation or pressure before, during or after the hearing.

When DODD issues the hearing officer's written recommendation (within ten calendar days) and the director's written decision (within five calendar days after that), the administrator gives copies to the board, enters the dates in the log, and implements the decision and every condition within the time the director sets. If the director sets no time, the administrator implements it promptly and documents the actions taken.

If the director's decision allows the transfer or termination, the administrator proceeds under TT-02 with the individual's service coordinator, the county board and the guardian. If the director rules for the individual or sets conditions, the administrator revises the plan, trains the staff involved and monitors compliance at least weekly for the first 30 days. The outcome is reported to the governing board at its next meeting.

The governing board reviews each appeal outcome and each instance of non-compliance as part of the internal compliance program (IC-01, GOV-01). A failure to follow this policy or the director's decision is treated as a serious compliance finding that may lead to adverse action under OAC 5123-3-06 (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Issues notices with appeal information, receives and logs appeals, meets the 5-day response deadline, sends certified mail, coordinates with DODD, represents the agency at mediation and hearing, and implements decisions.
Reviews appeals when assigned, ensures an impartial and timely decision, reviews outcomes and monitors non-compliance.
Give any appeal to the administrator the same day, help the individual to communicate, and never discourage or retaliate.
May appeal, attend mediation, request a hearing and choose supports to assist them at each step.
Participates in planning for any transfer and receives the notice and outcomes as required by TT-02.

documentation: Copy of the notice and proof of delivery date
Appeal Tracking Log with all deadlines and dates
The written appeal and its date-stamped receipt
Written outcome of the administrative review and certified mail receipts
DODD correspondence about the director-level appeal, mediation and hearing
Signed mediation agreement, if any (no mediation statements kept)
Hearing evidence file, hearing officer recommendation and director decision
Records of conditions imposed and actions taken to meet them
Governing board minutes reviewing the outcome

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Operator Duties and Policy Review
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing board, administrator, any contracted operator, and all staff of the residential facility and HCBS services
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, who is accountable for compliance with Chapter 5123-3 and other laws, and how this policy manual is kept current and reviewed.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is governed by a governing board that is responsible for the quality, safety and legal compliance of its services. The governing board will review annual audit or financial statements, review compliance review reports and plans of correction, monitor the internal compliance program and promote high-quality services.

If a licensee contracts with a separate entity to act as operator, there will be a written agreement requiring the operator to give the licensee the information the licensee needs to meet its obligations. The licensee stays responsible for compliance with all rules, whatever the contract says.

The operator will comply with Chapter 5123-3 and applicable federal, state and local law, including the Americans with Disabilities Act, fire code, wage and hour, workers' compensation, unemployment and withholding requirements. It will safeguard individuals' rights under ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65 and meet ORC 5123.63 and 5123.64 (see IC-03 and IR-01).

The agency maintains written policies and procedures on person-centered planning, individual satisfaction, internal monitoring, staff supervision, the training plan, service delivery, background investigations (OAC 5123-2-02) and, if volunteers are used, volunteers. This manual is reviewed at least annually and after any rule change, and every version is kept.

definitions.definition: The person or entity holding the DODD residential facility license.
The licensee or the entity contracted by the licensee that runs the facility day to day.
The body that holds ultimate authority and accountability for [AGENCY NAME].
The agency's process for finding, correcting and preventing non-compliance (see IC-01).
The written response to cited deficiencies after a compliance review (see GOV-04).

procedures: The governing board adopts, and records in its minutes, a list of members, officers and their terms. The board chair is [GOVERNING BOARD CHAIR]. The board meets at least quarterly, and the minutes record attendance, decisions and follow-up items.

The board appoints the administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) and approves written delegation of executive authority under AD-02. The organizational chart is updated within 30 days of any change and kept in the policy manual.

If [AGENCY NAME] uses a separate operator, the board approves a written agreement before services begin. The agreement requires the operator to give the licensee the information it needs (incidents, complaints, reviews, financial and staffing data) and states that the licensee remains responsible for compliance. The agreement is reviewed at each renewal.

Within 90 days after each fiscal year ends, the administrator or financial officer gives the board the annual audit or financial statements. The board reviews them, records questions and conclusions in the minutes, and confirms the financial proof requirements in GOV-03 are met.

Within 30 days of receiving a compliance review summary, report or plan of correction, the administrator gives the full document to the board. The board reviews the findings, the plan and progress on corrections at its next meeting, as described in GOV-04.

At least quarterly, the compliance officer ([COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME]) gives the board an internal compliance program report under IC-01. It covers incidents, billing audits, background check status, training completion, grievances and corrective actions. The board records its monitoring decisions in the minutes.

The board promotes high-quality services by reviewing the satisfaction and internal monitoring results under MP-02 at least annually, setting improvement goals and checking progress at later meetings.

The administrator maintains a legal compliance calendar with due dates for the ADA and accessibility review, annual fire inspection, wage and hour postings and payroll reviews (PS-02), workers' compensation and unemployment insurance renewals, and payroll tax withholding filings. The board receives confirmation of completion at least annually.

The administrator checks that required written policies exist for each topic named in OAC 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b): person-centered planning (MP-01), satisfaction and internal monitoring (MP-02), staff supervision (MP-03), the training plan (ST-04), service delivery (MP-04), background investigations (MP-05) and volunteers (DV-02) if volunteers are used.

The administrator reviews the whole policy manual at least annually, and within 60 days of any change in a relevant rule, statute, DODD guidance or agency practice. The review is recorded on the Policy Review Log, which shows the policy ID, date, reviewer, changes made and reason.

Each revised policy carries a version number and effective date. The prior version is archived with its dates of use. Superseded policies are never discarded while they could be relevant to a review period.

The board approves substantive policy changes and records its approval. The administrator then trains staff on any changes within 30 days, documents the training in personnel files (ST-03) and makes the current manual available to staff, individuals, guardians and surveyors on request.
The administrator ensures any contracted operator receives the current manual and each revision, and documents the operator's acknowledgment.

Conflict of interest: board members and the administrator disclose financial interests and related-party relationships annually in writing. Any change that must be reported to DODD is reported as described in GOV-03.

The administrator keeps a governance file with board minutes, bylaws, organizational chart, operator agreement, audit reports, review reports, policy review log and compliance calendar for surveyor review and for retention under RC-03.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews annual audit or financial statements and compliance review reports and plans of correction, monitors the internal compliance program, promotes high-quality services, and approves policy changes.
Runs daily operations, ensures legal compliance, maintains the compliance calendar, and performs and documents the annual policy review.
Prepares quarterly internal compliance reports for the board.
Gives the licensee the information it needs and complies with all Chapter 5123-3 requirements.
Follow current policies and report compliance concerns to the administrator.

documentation: Board roster, bylaws and minutes
Organizational chart
Written licensee/operator agreement (if applicable)
Annual audit or financial statements and board review notes
Compliance review reports and plans of correction with board review
Quarterly internal compliance reports
Legal compliance calendar and proof of completion
Policy Review Log, version history and archived versions
Staff training and acknowledgment records on policy changes

policies.title: Licensure, Licensed Capacity, Development Approval and Renewal
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing board, administrator and any person involved in admissions, development or renovation of the residential facility
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] obtains and keeps a valid DODD residential facility license, operates only within the terms of that license, and renews it on time.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will not operate a residential facility, or admit a person with a developmental disability to one, without a DODD license (ORC 5123.20). Before applying, it will obtain DODD development approval under OAC 5123-3-08, and DODD will not approve licensed beds exceeding the statutory limit. Applications are made to the DODD director under ORC 5123.19.

DODD conducts a pre-license survey and gives local officials notice. It cannot issue the license until 10 days (excluding weekends and holidays) after mailing. An initial license runs no longer than one year and renewals no longer than three years. DODD issues the three-year license within 20 days of compliance and fee collection, and issues a one-year license if an adverse action needs a plan of correction.

The license is valid only for the licensee, the named premises, the number of individuals on it and its term. It is not transferable, and the original is kept at the facility and shown to anyone on request. [AGENCY NAME] will never exceed the licensed capacity.

definitions.definition: DODD's approval, required before a license application, of the development or renovation of a residential facility under OAC 5123-3-08.
The number of individuals stated on the license.
DODD's on-site review of a facility before a license is issued.
The fee collected by DODD before the three-year license is issued, as set in the current LSC fee table.

procedures: Before any lease, purchase or renovation of a home, the administrator submits the development approval request to DODD under OAC 5123-3-08. The request is submitted before the license application, and no license application is filed until development approval is received in writing.

The administrator confirms with DODD in writing the controlling limit on licensed beds for the proposed facility, because bed-limit rules conflict across sources. The written confirmation is kept in the licensure file, and the planned capacity does not exceed it.

The administrator prepares the license application addressed to the DODD director. The application includes the licensee's legal name, the premises address ([ADDRESS]), the requested capacity, the administrator's information and proof of the financial and insurance requirements in GOV-03.

The administrator confirms the current fee with DODD before submission. As of 1/31/2025 the LSC table lists $100 initial and $300 three-year for 15 or fewer beds, and $500 initial and $1,500 three-year for 16 or more beds. The interim license has no fee. Payment is made on the schedule DODD sets, and the fee must be collected before the three-year license can issue.

The administrator confirms the home meets OAC 5123-3-02 standards (HE-01), the fire safety and emergency plan is approved (FS-01), staff are hired and trained (ST-04, ST-05) and policies are adopted (GOV-01) before the pre-license survey.

DODD conducts the pre-license survey and gives local officials notice. The administrator keeps a record of the notice mailing date, if DODD provides it, and does not expect the license to issue until 10 days (excluding weekends and holidays) after mailing.

No individual is admitted, and no person is accepted for services at the premises, until the license is received. The admissions coordinator checks the license in the licensure file before any admission under AM-01.

On receipt, the administrator checks the license for the correct licensee name, premises address, capacity and term, and reports any error to DODD within 3 business days. The administrator then records the expiration date on the compliance calendar and sets reminders at 180, 120 and 60 days before expiration.
The original license is displayed or kept at the facility and is shown to any person on request. A copy is kept in the licensure file at the administrative office.

The agency operates only for the licensee, at the named premises, within the licensed capacity and during the license term. It does not transfer, assign or lend the license. A change of licensee, premises or capacity requires contacting DODD in writing before acting, and any sale or transfer of operation follows RC-03 and DODD direction.

Before each admission, the admissions coordinator confirms current census plus the planned admission does not exceed licensed capacity, and the administrator signs the census check on the admission checklist.

At least 180 days before expiration, the administrator starts renewal. This includes a self-review against Chapter 5123-3, review of open plans of correction, confirmation of financial proof and insurance (GOV-03) and checking the current fee table with DODD. The administrator reports progress to the governing board.

The administrator tracks whether DODD issues a three-year license within 20 days of compliance and fee collection. If DODD issues a one-year license because an adverse action needs a plan of correction, the administrator follows GOV-04 and reports the plan and its progress to the board.

If the license is suspended, revoked or not renewed, the administrator stops admitting new individuals as directed, follows GOV-04 for notifying individuals and guardians within 3 business days, and works with the county board on transitions under TT-02.
The licensure file holds the application, development approval, fee receipts, license, renewal notices, DODD correspondence and capacity checks, kept under RC-03.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes the application and renewal, confirms funds for fees and financial proof, and reviews licensure status at each meeting.
Obtains development approval, files the application and renewal, tracks deadlines, posts the license and prevents operation beyond licensed terms.
Verifies a valid license and available capacity before any admission.
Includes licensure status and renewal readiness in the quarterly compliance report.

documentation: DODD development approval letter
Written confirmation of the controlling bed limit
License application and fee receipts
Pre-license survey correspondence and local official notice date
Original license and copies, with expiration reminders on the calendar
Census/capacity check on each admission checklist
Renewal self-review and DODD renewal correspondence
Board minutes about licensure

policies.title: Required Reports and Notifications to the State; Financial and Insurance Proof
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing board, administrator, delegate, and all staff who identify reportable events
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] makes every required report and notification to DODD and the county board on time, keeps its contact information current, and can prove its financial and insurance standing on request.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will notify DODD electronically within 14 days of disqualifying-offense charges or convictions, related-party status, a new financial interest of 5% or more, or an administrator license suspension, and within 7 days of bankruptcy. It will report an administrator change within 14 days and report if its administrator serves more than one licensee. It will keep its contact information with DODD current.

The agency will maintain a $10,000 line of credit or a $10,000 daily bank balance for 90 days, and general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 that includes individuals' theft and property-damage losses. Proof will be produced at application and on request. The same insurance and unencumbered $10,000 proof support agency provider certification under OAC 5123-2-08.

The agency will report any fire that results in a fire department response to DODD within 1 business day. It will notify the county board within 4 hours of discovering abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation, peer-to-peer acts, prohibited sexual relations, an unexplained death or a media inquiry, and submit the incident report by 3 p.m. on the next working day.

definitions.definition: An offense that bars or limits employment or licensure under the background investigation rules (see MP-05).
A person or entity related to the licensee as defined in the licensing rule, which must be reported to DODD.
A day other than a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.
Major unusual incident, reported under OAC 5123-17-02 and BP-03.
The reporting calendar and log kept by the administrator showing each deadline and its completion.

procedures: The administrator maintains the State Reporting Tracker. It lists each report type, deadline, responsible person, backup person, date discovered, date reported, method and confirmation. It covers the 14-day, 7-day, 1-business-day, 4-hour and next-working-day (3 p.m.) deadlines.
The administrator keeps DODD's contact record for the agency current. Any change of address, phone, email or contact person is sent to DODD electronically within 14 days and noted on the tracker.

Every year, and at each board reorganization, each board member, owner and the administrator completes a written disclosure covering: pending charges or convictions for a disqualifying offense, related-party relationships and any new financial interest of 5% or more. Ad hoc changes are disclosed to the administrator immediately.

When anyone discloses a charge or conviction for a disqualifying offense, a related-party relationship, a new 5%+ financial interest or an administrator license suspension, the administrator notifies DODD electronically within 14 days of the event. The tracker records the date of the event, the date reported and a copy of the confirmation.
If the agency or licensee files for bankruptcy, or a bankruptcy is filed against it, the administrator notifies DODD electronically within 7 days and informs the governing board at once.

When an administrator leaves, is replaced or is added, the licensee notifies DODD within 14 days of the change (see AD-01, AD-02). The administrator confirms the new administrator is not serving more than one licensee, or reports it to DODD if the person is.

The financial officer verifies each quarter that the licensee holds a line of credit of at least $10,000 or has held a daily bank balance of at least $10,000 for the past 90 days. The proof is in the licensee's name, unencumbered, and kept ready in the financial proof file (bank statements or the lender's letter).

The financial officer keeps a current general liability insurance certificate for at least $1,000,000 that covers individuals' theft and property-damage losses. The renewal date goes on the compliance calendar 90 days ahead. The insurance agent is asked to confirm in writing that the coverage includes those losses.

On request from DODD (or when applying or renewing under GOV-02, or for certification under OAC 5123-2-08), the administrator produces the financial and insurance proof within the time requested and records the request and response.

Fire reports: if a fire results in a fire department response, the administrator or on-call manager reports to DODD within 1 business day, in addition to emergency steps in FS-04. The report and confirmation are placed in the tracker and the incident file.

MUI county board notice: any staff member who discovers or suspects abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation, a peer-to-peer act, prohibited sexual relations, an unexplained death or receives a media inquiry tells the on-call manager immediately. The manager notifies the county board within 4 hours of discovery and records the time, name of the person notified and method.

Incident report: the administrator or designee submits the incident report by 3 p.m. on the next working day through the method DODD designates (see BP-03). If the next working day is a holiday or weekend, the deadline is the next day that is a working day.

Each Monday, the administrator reviews the tracker for open items. Each month, the compliance officer checks it against the incident log, personnel changes and the compliance calendar, and reports any late or missed report to the board chair within 2 business days.
A backup person is designated in writing for each report type, so that deadlines are met during the administrator's absence (see AD-02). The on-call phone number [PHONE] is posted for staff.
Staff are trained on these requirements at orientation and annually (ST-04, ST-01), and the training is documented.
The tracker, copies of all notifications and confirmations, and financial and insurance proof are retained under RC-03.

responsibilities.duty: Discloses reportable changes, ensures financial and insurance proof is maintained, and reviews tracker exceptions.
Makes all DODD notifications, maintains the tracker and DODD contact information, and produces proof on request.
Verifies the line of credit or bank balance and insurance certificate quarterly.
Makes the 4-hour county board notice and the 1-business-day fire report if the administrator is unavailable.
Report fires, suspected abuse, neglect or other MUIs and media inquiries immediately.

Copies and electronic confirmations of every DODD notice
Annual disclosure forms from board members, owners and the administrator
Line of credit letter or 90-day bank statements
General liability insurance certificate
Fire reports and MUI notification and incident report records
Monthly compliance officer check and board follow-up
Staff training records

policies.title: Compliance Reviews, Plans of Correction and Adverse Action
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing board, administrator, and all staff who may be asked to assist a DODD compliance review
policies.purpose: To prepare [AGENCY NAME] for DODD compliance reviews, to ensure timely appeals or plans of correction, and to protect individuals when DODD takes adverse action.
policies.policy:
DODD reviews the facility at least once per license term, and special reviews may be unannounced. [AGENCY NAME] will cooperate fully, give reviewers access to the premises, individuals, staff and records, and will never obstruct or retaliate.

DODD issues a written summary within 10 days of the review ending. The agency will appeal or submit a plan of correction within 14 days of receipt. DODD acts within 10 days on an appeal and within 20 days on a plan of correction.

Adverse actions include suspension of admissions, placement of a monitor, and refusal to renew or revocation of the license. A one-year license may be issued if an adverse action needs a plan of correction. The agency will notify individuals and guardians within 3 business days of any adverse action.

definitions.definition: A DODD review of the facility's compliance with Chapter 5123-3, which may be scheduled or unannounced (a special review).
DODD's written findings issued within 10 days of the review ending.
The agency's written plan showing how and when each cited deficiency will be corrected.
Suspension of admissions, placement of a monitor, or refusal to renew or revocation of the license.

procedures: The administrator maintains a review-ready file: license, policies, training records, personnel files, drill records, incident logs, individual records and inspection reports. The compliance officer performs a self-review at least annually using Chapter 5123-3 and records the results (IC-01).

A review may be unannounced. Any staff member who is approached by a DODD reviewer greets the reviewer courteously, asks for identification, notifies the administrator or on-call manager at [PHONE] immediately and does not delay access. In the administrator's absence, the delegate under AD-02 acts.

During the review, the administrator or delegate provides records and access, accompanies the reviewers where appropriate, answers questions truthfully, and keeps notes of what was requested and provided. Staff and individuals are told they may speak with reviewers freely. No one is coached or pressured.
At the exit meeting, the administrator records the reviewers' preliminary observations, asks for clarification, and corrects any immediate health and safety issues the same day.

On receipt of the written summary (DODD issues it within 10 days of the review ending), the administrator date-stamps it, enters the receipt date and the 14-day deadline on the compliance calendar, and gives a copy to the board chair within 2 business days.

The administrator and compliance officer review each finding within 3 business days and decide with the board chair whether to submit a plan of correction or appeal. A finding may be appealed where the agency has documented evidence that it is wrong.

The plan of correction or appeal is submitted to DODD within 14 days of receipt of the summary. Each cited item in the plan states the corrective steps, the person responsible, the completion date, how recurrence will be prevented and how the agency will monitor effectiveness.

The administrator keeps proof of timely submission. DODD acts within 10 days on an appeal and within 20 days on a plan, and the administrator logs those dates and follows up with DODD if no response is received.
If DODD does not accept the plan or requests changes, the administrator revises and resubmits within the time DODD gives, and informs the board chair.

The administrator implements each corrective step by the date in the plan and assigns a staff member to verify it. Training given as a correction is documented with sign-in sheets and competency checks (ST-04). Evidence of completion is placed in the review file.

The compliance officer checks each corrected item again at 30 and 90 days after correction, and reports results to the governing board. The board reviews each review report and plan of correction and monitors progress until all items are closed (GOV-01).

If DODD takes an adverse action (suspension of admissions, a monitor, or refusal to renew or revocation), the administrator informs the board chair the same day. Within 3 business days, the administrator notifies each individual and guardian in writing, in accessible language and format (IR-01), and offers to explain it in person.

During a suspension of admissions, the admissions coordinator stops all admissions, tells referral sources and the county board, and records the effective date. If a monitor is placed, the administrator gives the monitor full access to the facility, records and staff.

If the agency faces refusal to renew or revocation, the administrator gets legal advice, protects individuals' continuity of care by working with the county board and guardians (TT-02), and preserves all records under RC-03. Any appeal rights under the DODD notice are calendared on the day the notice is received.
If the agency receives a one-year license because an adverse action needs a plan of correction, the administrator tracks the plan closely and prepares for renewal under GOV-02.

The administrator keeps a Compliance Review File for each review with the summary, plan or appeal, DODD responses, evidence of correction, notices to individuals and guardians, and board minutes, and retains it under RC-03.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews each report and plan of correction, monitors progress to closure and authorizes appeals.
Prepares for reviews, hosts reviewers, meets the 14-day deadline, implements corrections and sends 3-business-day adverse action notices.
Performs annual self-reviews and verifies corrective actions at 30 and 90 days.
Acts for the administrator during an unannounced review.
Cooperate with reviewers, answer truthfully and notify the administrator immediately.
